key: FROM Fervour kindled to its height Eternal Law and Truth were born: Thence was the Night produced, and thence the billowy flood of sea arose.
s: Opening a three-verse hymn of origins that ends with the Creator forming sun, moon, heaven and earth; Sāyaṇa, on 10.190.1, takes ‘Law’ as true intention and ‘Truth’ as true speech, both born of the fervour Brahmā spent before creation contemplating what he would make.

evidence.words: ऋतमिति सत्यनाम । ऋतं मानसं यथार्थसंकल्पनं सत्यं वाचिकं यथार्थभाषणम् । चकाराभ्यामन्यदपि शास्त्रीयं धर्मजातं समुच्चीयते । तत्सर्वमभीद्धादभितप्ताद्ब्रह्मणा पुरा सृष्ट्यर्थं कृतात्तपसोऽधि । अध्युपर्यर्थे । उपर्यजायत । उदपद्यत । ‘ तपस्तप्त्वेदं सर्वमसृजत ' (तै. आ. ८. ६ ) इति श्रुतेः । तपश्चात्र स्रष्टव्यपर्यालोचनलक्षणम् ।
evidence.gloss: Ṛta is a name for truth: ṛta is of the mind, a true intention; satya is of speech, a true statement. The two “and”s take in the rest of the duties the scriptures teach. All this arose from the kindled tapas performed of old by Brahmā for the sake of creation (“having done tapas he created all this”, Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 8.6). Tapas here has the character of contemplating what is to be created.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 10.190.1, at [1026,1]). Plain sense faithful: 10.190 has three verses and verse 3 has Dhatar the Creator forming sun, moon, heaven, earth; no four-word overlap. Sāyaṇa on 10.190.1 says ṛta is mental true resolve and satya verbal true speech, born of tapas done by Brahmā of old for creation, tapas being the contemplation of what is to be created. ब्रह्मणा could grammatically be neuter brahman, but Wilson’s note reports Sāyaṇa as alluding to the penance of Brahmā preceding creation, and सृष्ट्यर्थं ... तपस्तप्त्वेदं सर्वमसृजत fits the creator; ‘before creation’ matches पुरा and Wilson’s ‘preceding creation’. Sāyaṇa’s alternative (यद्वा: from the radiant supreme Self) is not claimed. entry-check ok, 44 words.
